problem.park: Hip-exoskeleton controllers that generalise across speeds and slopes usually need motion-capture data and biomechanical labels. Park et al. train a hip-exo policy entirely in a predictive neuromusculoskeletal simulation, without motion imitation. The teacher sees privileged simulator state and learns muscle excitations and hip torques jointly. It is distilled into a student that uses only a thigh gyroscope and runs on hardware. The paper evaluates (i) simulation fidelity against open human data, (ii) simulated effort reduction against a matched no-exo policy, and (iii) whether the torque waveform survives transfer to hardware (pp1-3).
problem.choi: The question is whether a musculoskeletal imitation policy can be fine-tuned with RL into 'device-agnostic' hip or ankle exo policies. The policy tracks one subject's walking and running kinematics and kinetics. The resulting policies should cut simulated metabolic cost for able-bodied gait and give deficit-specific (asymmetric) assistance for simulated unilateral muscle weakness, with no human trials (pp1-2). 'Personalised' means specific to a simulated deficit. The policy is not fitted to an individual wearer's data. Simulation only; no hardware.

park_teacher.simulator: [config] Hyfydy physics inside SCONE. The control policy runs at 40 Hz and forward dynamics are 'integrated at 200 Hz' (p3 Sec II-A). Walk-RL implements this as fixed_control_step_size = 0.005 in every .scone file plus a wrapper step_size of 0.025 s, so excitations are held for 5 substeps.
park_teacher.human_model: [config] H2190 full body with the upper limbs removed: 21 DoF and 90 Hill-type muscles with first-order activation dynamics. 80 muscles act on the legs (40 per leg; 6 DoF per leg: hip 3, knee 1, ankle 2) and 10 on the pelvis and torso (torso 3 DoF) (p3 Sec II-A-1, Fig 2 p2). Model mass 74.5 kg (p5 Eq 4). [derived-ours] The body masses in Walk-RL model/H2190v2k.hfd sum to 74.53 kg.
park_teacher.device_model: [config] Bilateral hip flexion-extension torque actuators, added in curriculum stage 2. Added masses: 0.5 kg per thigh, 2.0 kg pelvis and 1.3 kg torso, 4.3 kg in total. Segment inertia is scaled in proportion to the added mass. Result: 90 muscle actuators plus 2 exo actuators (p3 Sec II-A-1).
park_teacher.torque_path: [config] Raw command u_cmd goes through a causal first-order low-pass filter: u_k = u_{k-1} + alpha*(u_cmd,k - u_{k-1}) with alpha = dt/tau_LPF (Eqs 1-2, p3). The paper defines dt as 'the simulation time step' and sets tau_LPF = 0.1 s. Peak actuator torque magnitude is capped at 12 Nm (p3). Reward term r_sm also penalises the squared finite difference of successive left and right exo commands (p4). The order of clip and filter is not stated.
park_teacher.action_space: [config] 32 inputs: 10 synergy coefficients per leg (20), 10 direct torso and pelvis activations, and 2 hip torque commands. In the no-exo branch the torque commands are clamped to zero (p3-4 Sec II-A-3). Synergies come from human overground walking data (kinematics plus GRFs). OpenSim Moco (MocoInverse) on an OpenSim-converted H2190 estimates activations, and NMF on the right-leg activation matrix gives a fixed synergy weight matrix (p3). The synergy data came from Jooeun Ahn's group (Acknowledgment p9). [code, Walk-RL] Actions in [-1,1] map to [0,1] via 0.5*(a+1). Leg excitations = a_syn . (1.5*W), with W a 10x40 non-negative matrix (max entry 1.537 after the 1.5 factor). The same W serves both legs, and everything is clipped to [0,1]. Optional 'use_symmetry' swaps the left and right action and observation blocks when the last foot strike was left (contact force y > 1 N). The paper never mentions this swap.
park_teacher.observation: [config] Muscle fibre length, velocity, force and excitation for all muscles; joint positions and velocities; head orientation and angular velocity; relative positions of both feet; GRF under each foot, all normalised. Also the current bilateral hip-exo torques (normalised by max torque), whole-body COM velocity and target speed (p4 Sec II-A-4). [derived-ours from Walk-RL] The public layout has 515 dims: 5x90 muscle arrays (fibre length, fibre velocity, force, excitation, activation), head quaternion 4, head angular velocity 3, feet relative to pelvis 6, DoF positions 21 (pelvis translations zeroed), DoF velocities 21, GRF/BW 6, COM velocity 3, target speed 1. SB3 VecNormalize(norm_obs=True, norm_reward=False).
park_teacher.reward: [config] Eq 3 (p4): r = w_vel*r_vel + w_eff*r_eff + w_rom*r_rom + w_sm*r_sm + w_fall*r_fall + w_knee*r_knee + w_front*r_front. The terms are defined in the paper (p4) but no weight is reported. (a) r_vel: product of Gaussians of forward and vertical COM velocity, head orientation and head angular velocity, with a flat band around target speed. (b) r_eff: sum of squared muscle activations. (c) r_rom: knee beyond 0 deg and lumbar extension outside [-30, 2.5] deg. (d) r_knee: stance knee load above 3 body weights. (e) r_front: squared hip adduction angles on both sides. (f) r_sm: squared difference of successive exo torque commands. (g) r_fall: one-time large penalty when COM height falls below a relative threshold. [code, Walk-RL; no exo, so a precursor only] Only four terms exist, with weights gaussian_vel 10, effort -0.1, rom -25, fall -250. r_vel = r_vx * r_head_angvel * r_vz, each term exp(-0.06*x^2/sigma^2). sigma_vx = 0.07 m/s measured from the edge of a +/-0.05 m/s flat band; sigma_vz = 0.1; head angular velocity sigma = (0.6, 0.65, 1.4) rad/s. Head orientation is computed but left out of the product. rom = knee_r + knee_l violations above 0 rad + lumbar violation outside [-20, +10] deg. fall = 1 if COM y < 3 (absolute; terrain sits at y about 5) or COM height above the lower calcaneus < 0.5 m. The knee-load, frontal and smoothness terms are absent.
park_teacher.curriculum_and_randomisation: [config] Each episode draws one slope from 11 values (-5 to +5 deg in 1-deg steps), via a categorical distribution over per-slope difficulty scores. Scores start uniform; a fall raises the score, a success lowers it, with a floor. Target speed follows a cyclic list 0.7 -> 1.5 -> 0.7 m/s across episodes (ref [35], MetaMobilityLabCMU/speed-adaptive-agent) (p4 Sec II-A-5). [code, Walk-RL] Different: 10,000 pre-generated terrains of 50 tiles, each 1 m long with an integer slope uniform in -6..+6 deg per tile; a speed list of 20 entries 0.7..1.6..0.7 m/s, advanced at every reset; episode cap 1000 steps (25 s at 40 Hz).
park_teacher.training: [config] Table I (p2): SB3 SAC, MlpPolicy, actor and critic [512, 512, 256], 30 parallel envs. Stage 1: steps 0-5e7, exo zero-clamped, LR linear 1e-3 -> 0. Stage 2: steps 5e7-1e8 run as two parallel branches: (i) exo policy-controlled and (ii) exo zero-clamped for the same number of steps. The LR schedule is reset to linear 5e-4 -> 0 for both. gamma 0.99, replay 3e6, batch 512, target tau 0.005, ent_coef 'auto_0.1' (SB3 syntax: auto-tuned from 0.1). [derived-ours] Total env steps = 5e7 + 2*5e7 = 1.5e8. [code, Walk-RL main] ReLU; gSDE on (use_sde=True, sde_sample_freq=1); learning_starts 1e4; train_freq 4; gradient_steps 4; target_update_interval 1; ent_coef 'auto'; 20 SubprocVecEnv envs; 75M steps; batch 256; tau 0.02; LR 1e-3 linear. [code, NMSM branch] Batch 512, tau 0.01, LR 5e-4, 6 synergies ('251204_NMSM_Inv_6'), symmetry off. Neither branch matches Table I.

park_student.sensor_selection: [measured-hw vs sim] Simulated femur angular velocity in the femur frame is compared with a thigh-bar IMU while 'a participant' walked for 1 min at 1.2 m/s on level ground. Axes are defined in upright standing: x anteroposterior, y vertical, z mediolateral. z: r 0.55, RMSE 96.0 deg/s. x: r -0.19, RMSE 41.2 deg/s. y: r -0.25, RMSE 60.9 deg/s. z was chosen on correlation alone, although it had the largest RMSE (p4 Sec II-B, Fig 3).
park_student.data: [config] Teacher rollouts on level ground, +5 deg and -5 deg over a range of target speeds, with constant-speed trials and smoothly varying-speed trials. 'During rollouts, the controller operated at 100 Hz' (p4). Each sample pairs the teacher's instantaneous right-hip torque command with a 0.95 s (95-sample) history of right femur mediolateral angular velocity (p4-5). Dataset size, split unit and normalisation are not reported.
park_student.model_and_training: [config] Temporal convolutional network (TCN), single channel in, right-hip torque out. MSE loss, 5 epochs, with a held-out validation set. Training loss 7.45e-2 -> 4.99e-2 and validation loss 8.23e-2 -> 6.54e-2, in normalised torque units [-1,1] (p5). The TCN architecture, optimiser and batch size are not reported.
park_student.open_loop_check: [measured-sim] Fig 4 (p5) shows one level-ground trial at 0.7/1.1/1.5 m/s (text: 4 s each; caption and axis: 5 s each). The student tracks the teacher with R^2 = 0.93, and nothing is output for the first 0.95 s while the history fills. No closed-loop student-in-simulation result is reported.
park_student.inconsistency: Sec II intro (p3) says the student receives 'bilateral femur mediolateral angular velocity'. Sec II-B (p4-5) trains a right-only, unilateral mapping. The left-hip mapping (mirroring, sign) is not described.

park_deployment.hardware: [config] Robotic hip exo, 4.5 kg, joint torque up to 18 Nm in the sagittal plane. Two quasi-direct-drive AK80-9 motors (CubeMars), ICM20948 IMUs on the distal thigh bars, 22.2 V 3300 mAh LiPo, Jetson Orin Nano. The student is converted to TensorRT and runs at 100 Hz, with separate I/O and inference processes (IMUs on I2C, actuators on CAN; Fig 5b) (p5 Sec II-C).
park_deployment.command_chain: [config] u_scaled = u_cmd * m_subject/74.5 (Eq 4). tau_LPF = 0.15 s on hardware vs 0.1 s in simulation, 'to better attenuate measurement noise and inter-subject gait variability'. Rate limiter u'_t = clip(u_t, u_{t-1} - c, u_{t-1} + c), c = 0.5 (p5). Units of c and the order of scaling, clip, rate limit and filter are not stated. If c is in Nm per 10 ms step it caps slew at 50 Nm/s; if it is in normalised units it is essentially non-binding [derived-ours].

choi_base_imitation.simulator: [config] Hyfydy with the SCONE Python API: physics 200 Hz, policy 25 Hz, contacts with nonlinear damping and dynamic plus viscous friction (p2 Sec II-A-1). No MyoSuite or MuJoCo model is used anywhere.
choi_base_imitation.human_model: [config] Hyfydy 3D H2190: 21 DoF, 90 muscles, with tendon elasticity, pennation and fibre damping (p2 Sec II-A-2, ref [29] Schumacher et al. 2025). This is the same body as Park.
choi_base_imitation.reference_data: [config] One subject from the Scherpereel et al. 2023 Sci Data dataset (12 participants, 31 activities): a treadmill clip of about 2 minutes covering five speeds from 0.6 to 2.2 m/s. Fig 2 shows walking at 0.6/1.2/1.8 m/s and running at 2.0/2.2 m/s. Belt velocity, estimated from toe markers during stance, is added to convert to overground. OpenSim IK/ID give reference joint angles and moments plus head, pelvis and feet positions. The clip is duplicated and mirrored across the sagittal plane (p3 Sec II-B). Which subject is not stated.
choi_base_imitation.rl_formulation: [config] DeepMimic-style (ref [31]). A = [-1,1]^96: 90 muscle excitations mapped linearly to [0,1], plus 6 normalised sagittal torques at bilateral hip, knee and ankle. The torques are clamped to 0 except during exo fine-tuning. Excitation -> activation uses first-order forward Euler inside Hyfydy (p3 Sec II-C-1). The observation is in R^839: S_c (fibre length, force, activation; GRFs; joint angles; root and feet linear velocities) plus S_f = (Theta_{t+k} - Theta_t) for k = 1..5. The text says 'next four reference frames', inconsistent with k = 1..5 (p3 Sec II-C-2).
choi_base_imitation.reward: [config] Eq 1 (p3): r = w_pos r_pos + w_vel r_vel + w_root r_root + w_ee r_ee + w_torq r_torq - w_eff r_eff - w_smt r_smt - w_exo r_exo. The tracking terms (pos, vel, root, ee, torq) are each exp(k * squared error): pos over all 21 DoF including root orientation; vel on joint velocities; root on the pelvis position; ee on feet and head positions; torq against inverse-dynamics joint torques (Eqs 2-6). r_eff = Edot = hdot_AM + hdot_SL + wdot_CE is a metabolic probe after Umberger 2003 and Uchida 2016, with fast-twitch fractions from refs [34-36] and other parameters at Hyfydy defaults (Eq 7). r_smt = (1/N)*sum_m (e_t - e_{t-1})^2 on excitations (Eq 8). r_exo = 0.5*sum_{L,R} |tau_exo|/tau_max (Eq 9). Table II (p4), base / fine-tune: k_pos -2.0/-0.4, k_vel -0.05/-0.01, k_root -500/-500, k_ee -80/-16, k_torq -2.0/-0.4. Weights are identical in both columns: w_pos 0.25, w_vel 0.1, w_root 0.15, w_ee 0.25, w_torq 0.25, w_smo -1.0. Effort weight w_eff -3e-5 (base) vs -3e-4 (fine-tune); w_exo absent (base) vs -0.2 (fine-tune). The table lists penalty weights as negative while Eq 1 subtracts them, a sign ambiguity; the intended reading is surely a penalty.
choi_base_imitation.training: [config] Table III (p4): SB3 SAC, actor and twin-Q [512, 512, 256], batch 256, LR linear decay from 3e-4, soft update 0.02, entropy auto, gamma 0.95, train freq 4, gradient steps 4, target update interval 1. Base policy 600M steps; each fine-tune 150M. 96 parallel envs on an RTX 5090 + Intel (Core) Ultra 9 285K workstation, about 48 h for the base policy (p4 Sec II-D-1). Episodes use reference-state initialisation at a uniformly sampled clip time, with the vertical position adjusted so net GRF equals body weight. Episodes are truncated at 250 steps (10 s) and terminate early when the root is more than 0.4 m from the reference root (p4-5).

mechanism_exact.choi_exo_finetune: [config] Each device condition fine-tunes the base policy for another 150M steps, with the exo action space enabled; hip and ankle policies are trained separately. The four tracking gains are loosened 5x and w_eff is raised 10x (Table II). Device mass and inertia are added: hip exo 2.9 kg (pelvis 1.5, 0.7 per thigh); ankle exo 3.9 kg (pelvis 1.5, 1.0 per shank, 0.2 per foot). Totals come from OpenExo (ref [30]), split 'using a heuristic approach', with inertia scaled proportionally (Table I p3; p2 and p5). Output in [-1,1] is mapped to [-tau_max, tau_max]. The rate of change is clipped at tau_max per step, then a first-order LPF is applied with cutoff 1 Hz for the hip (tau = 0.159 s) or 2 Hz for the ankle (tau = 0.080 s) (p5 Sec II-D-2). tau_max is never reported. The knee motor exists in the action space, but no knee policy is reported.
mechanism_exact.choi_impaired: [config] Unilateral plantarflexor weakness or hip-flexor weakness: the maximum excitation of the affected group is set to 5% of baseline. The policy is fine-tuned with the same reward changes as the exo fine-tune. Weakness plus the exo action space is then trained jointly, still tracking the healthy reference (p5 Sec II-D-3). The muscle lists per group are not given. Stated hypothesis: imitating healthy gait with a weakened model plus exo yields compensating torque profiles (p5).

protocol.park_sim_fidelity: [measured-sim] The stage-2 no-exo policy (Fig 6 caption, p6) is compared with Reznick et al. 2021 open data on sagittal hip, knee and ankle angles and moments, at 3 slopes and 3 speeds (0.8, 1.0, 1.2 m/s) (p6-7 Sec III-A). The exo-assisted gait is never validated against human data.
protocol.park_sim_effect: [measured-sim] Exo branch vs no-exo branch at 3 slopes x 9 speeds (0.7-1.5 m/s in 0.1 steps, per the Fig 9 axis). Metrics: mean activation over all muscles in a 15 s segment, and mean positive joint power. The Fig 9 caption says hip, knee and ankle bilateral, sagittal; the text says 'hip-knee'. Effects are reported as % change 'related to no-exoskeleton', averaged over speed (p7 Sec III-C). Seeds, episodes per condition and the definition of joint power (biological vs total) are not reported.
protocol.park_profile_timing: [measured-sim] The learned level-ground profile at 1.2 m/s is compared on peak timing only with a spline controller at 1.25 m/s (ref [37]) and a delayed bio-torque profile (ref [15]; mean of 20 cycles x 20 participants with a 125 ms delay) (p7 Sec III-B, Fig 7). No performance comparison is made.

park_human.design: [measured-hw] N=5 able-bodied (4 M, 1 F; 71.62 +/- 8.89 kg), CMU IRB STUDY2024_00000506 (p5 Sec II-D). Five minutes of acclimation at 1.2 m/s with the exo powered, on an instrumented split-belt treadmill (Bertec FIT5). Slopes 0, +5 and -5 deg; within each, speed rises 0.7 -> 1.5 m/s in 0.2 steps at 30 s per speed. The paper says 3 min 30 s per condition, but 5 x 30 s = 2 min 30 s. GRFs are used only for gait events. Onboard exo 'hip-torque commands were logged'. Five consecutive cycles per speed-slope condition are normalised to 101 points (p6). r and RMSE against the simulated profile are computed per speed-slope condition (p7 Sec III-D).
park_human.shows: [measured-hw] With the IMU-only TCN running on a Jetson at 100 Hz, right-hip torque waveforms normalised to the gait cycle keep the simulated shape. r = 0.82 +/- 0.19 overall; 0.98 uphill, 0.83 level, 0.66 downhill. RMSE is about 0.02-0.04 Nm/kg against peaks of about 0.1 Nm/kg (Fig 10, p8).
park_human.does_not_show: Delivered torque: the protocol logs commands, even though Results says 'measured', and no torque sensor or calibration is reported. Any effect on the wearer: no metabolic, EMG, kinematics, comfort or preference data, and no zero-torque or no-device condition. Per-participant results and statistics. The left hip. Overground, transient or non-cyclic tasks. Latency. Robustness to sensor placement. Retention of the simulated effort savings. The authors' own project page says the controller 'fails to provide effective assistance during ramp descent' (IlseungPark/Learning-Hip-Exo index.html @ b8ec147).

protocol.choi_eval: [measured-sim] (1) Tracking against the same single-subject reference used in training: angles, moments and GRF averaged over 10 cycles; moments low-pass filtered (4th-order zero-lag Butterworth, 4 Hz) (Fig 2 caption p5). This is in-sample fit, not held-out prediction. (2) Metabolic-probe cost for no-exo, hip exo and ankle exo at 5 speeds (Fig 4a), and averages over the walking speeds (0.6/1.2/1.8) and running speeds (2.0/2.2) (Fig 4b). (3) Assistance profiles compared visually with experimentally optimised splines (refs [13], [39], [40]) (Fig 3). (4) Impaired models at 1.2 m/s: kinematics, asymmetry of assistance, metabolic cost and bilateral symmetry RMSE (Figs 5-7). How the no-exo baseline was trained, and whether it carries device mass, is not stated. [derived-ours] Fig 4b draws one shared No-Exo bar for both devices, although the devices differ in mass (2.9 vs 3.9 kg), so the baseline most likely carries no device mass.

headline_numbers.what: Mean muscle activation, exo vs matched no-exo, averaged over speed
headline_numbers.value: -1.1% level, -3.4% ramp ascent (reductions); ramp descent 'changing by -2.2%'
headline_numbers.where: p7 Sec III-C; Fig 9 p7; abstract p1 ('up to 3.4%')
headline_numbers.caveat: [derived-ours] In Fig 9, positive values mean reduction (level ground averages about +1 and the text calls it a 1.1% reduction). The ramp-descent -2.2% is therefore an increase in activation. Activation rose with assistance at 7/9 descent speeds, 3/9 level and 2/9 ascent speeds, mostly the slow ones (figure reading, approximate). The % basis (relative?) is unspecified; one policy per branch; no variance reported.

headline_numbers.what: Mean positive joint power, exo vs matched no-exo
headline_numbers.caveat: The text says 'hip-knee' power; the Fig 9 caption says hip, knee and ankle. Whether this is biological or total joint power is not defined.

headline_numbers.what: Speed dependence of benefit (Pearson r vs speed, 'pooled across slopes')
headline_numbers.caveat: [derived-ours] Values read from Fig 9 reproduce r of about 0.975 only if slopes are averaged per speed (n = 9). All 27 points pooled give about 0.69. Power gave about 0.68 at n = 9 against the paper's 0.76 (figure reading).

headline_numbers.what: Simulation fidelity (no-exo) against Reznick et al. 2021, 3 slopes x 0.8/1.0/1.2 m/s
Peak timing of learned profile (level, 1.2 m/s) vs references
headline_numbers.value: Extension peak 17% GC (spline 9%, bio-torque 13%); flexion peak 71% (both references 61%)

headline_numbers.what: Lag of exo torque behind the biological hip moment
headline_numbers.value: Moment peaks at 6.9% (ext) and 55.4% (flex) GC; torque peaks at 18.6% and 74.1%; lag 103 ms (ext) and 166 ms (flex)
headline_numbers.where: p7 Sec III-B; Fig 8 p7; Discussion p9
headline_numbers.caveat: [derived-ours] The tau = 0.1 s first-order LPF alone delays a 0.9 Hz stride fundamental by about 91 ms (see rival_explanations).

headline_numbers.what: Thigh gyro agreement, sim vs hardware (1 participant, 1 min, 1.2 m/s, level)
headline_numbers.caveat: Selection used correlation only; z has the largest RMSE.

headline_numbers.value: Train MSE 7.45e-2 -> 4.99e-2; validation 8.23e-2 -> 6.54e-2 (normalised units [-1,1], 5 epochs); representative trial R^2 = 0.93
headline_numbers.caveat: [derived-ours] Validation RMSE is about 0.256 of full scale, about 3.1 Nm if full scale is 12 Nm. Against a +/-6 Nm sinusoid that corresponds to an aggregate R^2 of about 0.5 (assumption-laden). The showcased 0.93 trial is probably better than average. Open-loop only.

headline_numbers.what: Sim vs hardware right-hip torque waveforms (5 participants, 15 speed-slope conditions, 5 cycles each)
headline_numbers.where: p7-8 Sec III-D; Fig 10 p8; abstract p1
headline_numbers.caveat: Commands, not sensed torque (protocol p6). r ignores amplitude. What the +/- spans across (conditions or participants) is not stated. [derived-ours, visual] At level ground, hardware flexion peaks sit around 80-85% GC against about 65-75% in simulation.

headline_numbers.value: 40 Hz control / 200 Hz dynamics; 12 Nm cap; tau_LPF 0.1 s (sim) and 0.15 s (hw); rate limit c = 0.5; mass scaling m/74.5 kg; 95-sample (0.95 s) window at 100 Hz; 50M + 50M(x2) SAC steps; 30 envs
headline_numbers.where: p3 Sec II-A; p5 Sec II-B/II-C, Eq 4; Table I p2
headline_numbers.caveat: Training hardware and wall-clock not reported.

headline_numbers.value: Angle RMSE: hip 2.85, knee 4.03, ankle 3.68 deg; R^2 0.97, 0.97, 0.85
Moment RMSE 0.10, 0.10, 0.11 Nm/kg (R^2 0.94, 0.87, 0.97); GRF RMSE 0.14 BW, R^2 0.95 'despite the agent having no access to GRF data'
headline_numbers.caveat: GRF is largely implied by tracking kinematics plus ID moments (argued-ours).

headline_numbers.what: Gross metabolic reduction vs no-exo baseline
headline_numbers.value: Hip: 4.57% walking, 6.95% running. Ankle: 6.15% walking, 13.81% running. Reductions at every speed, larger at higher speeds
headline_numbers.caveat: [derived-ours, by eye] No-exo is about 5.5 W/kg (mean of 0.6/1.2/1.8 m/s) walking and about 10.35 W/kg (mean of 2.0/2.2 m/s) running. 'Running' means 2.0-2.2 m/s. Baseline training and mass not specified.

ablations_that_matter: Park reports no ablations. There is no synergy vs direct-muscle exo teacher, filter tau or torque-cap sweep, reward-term ablation, curriculum ablation, seed replication, student window, architecture or sensor ablation beyond the axis correlation, or sensor-noise randomisation. The matched no-exo branch (Table I; p3) is a control, not an ablation. It is the design element most worth copying.

Park's Fig 7 compares spline and delayed bio-torque references on peak timing only. The ablation that matters, the effort benefit of the same references run through the same simulated device, is missing (p7 Sec III-B).

[code evidence] Walk-RL has 'ind' (all 90 muscles) vs 'syn' (synergy) configs and 10-seed scripts (commit f9042a9, seeds 10-19). That comparison belongs to the companion paper arXiv 2603.10474, not to the exo paper; no exo-condition synergy ablation exists.

Choi reports no ablations: no reward-only control, seeds, tau_max, filter or device-mass variation. The most important missing control is a no-exo fine-tune with the identical reward change (5x looser tracking, 10x effort weight), the same 150M steps and the same device mass. Without it, part of the 4.6-13.8% probe reduction may come from the reward change rather than the torque (see rival_explanations).
Choi's hip vs ankle and able-bodied vs impaired comparisons are condition comparisons, not ablations. Knee motors exist in the action space, but no knee policy is reported.

For our programme, these ablations are cheap and decisive. (1) Paired seeds per arm (exo vs matched zero-torque). (2) A filter-tau sweep, to test whether the 'learned' lag follows the filter. (3) A closed-loop student vs teacher run in simulation. (4) Command vs delivered torque on the bench. (5) A reward-change-only fine-tune whenever the reward changes between stages.
limitations_admitted: Park p9: 'the human evaluation was not intended as a rigorous efficacy study'.
Park p9: the controller targets cyclic locomotion and has not been validated for non-cyclic or unstructured behaviour.
Park p9: a single-axis thigh gyro may be insufficient for broader contexts and sensitive to sensor-placement variability.

Park p9: 'we did not explicitly optimize domain randomization and adaptation strategies'. Future work: match sensor noise and mounting dynamics, add richer sensing, use sim-to-real robustness objectives during distillation.

Park p8: minimal benefit in simulation on ramp descent (explained by negative-work biomechanics). Project page (b8ec147): the controller 'fails to provide effective assistance during ramp descent, suggesting that a sim-to-real gap still remains'.
Choi p7: policies 'have not yet been deployed or validated on physical hardware'; distillation (ref [20] = Park) is proposed.
Choi p7-8: the impaired models may not capture the full complexity of real pathological gait; patient experiments are required.
Choi p7: peak torques applied to the impaired-gait models 'may exceed the current mechanical capabilities of lightweight portable devices'.
Choi p8: the study covers only level-ground walking and running.
limitations_not_admitted: Park: a single training run per branch, apparently (no seeds or variance). The 1.1-3.4% activation effects compare two separately trained policies, so seed-to-seed variance is confounded with the exo effect.
Park: at slow speeds, assistance increased activation on all three slopes, and ramp descent shows a net increase (Fig 9, sign convention derived by us). The text calls descent a 'modest benefit'.

Park: the student is evaluated only open-loop against teacher rollouts. The closed-loop effect of the student on simulated effort is never reported, and hardware measures no effort. So there is no evidence that the savings survive distillation or transfer.

Park: the hardware comparison uses logged commands (p6), although Results calls them 'measured'. r ignores amplitude. Nm/kg normalisation cancels the mass scaling. The hardware filter (0.15 s) and rate limiter differ from simulation, so 'without additional hardware tuning' (abstract) holds only narrowly.

Park: the validation loss (6.54e-2 normalised) implies aggregate distillation error far larger than the showcased R^2 0.93 (derived). Dataset size and split unit are unknown, so window leakage cannot be ruled out.
Park: the gyro axis was chosen on one participant and 1 minute of walking. r = 0.55 is moderate, and the chosen axis has the largest RMSE (96 deg/s).

Park: the reported 103-166 ms lag is interpreted as learned, phase-dependent timing (p9). A first-order LPF with tau = 0.1 s produces about 90 ms of lag at walking stride frequency by itself (derived), and the paper does not discuss this.
Park: effort is scored as mean activation, and the reward directly penalises summed squared activation, so the metric is not independent. No metabolic model is used.
Park: the paper does not say whether the device mass is present in the no-exo branch, or whether the replay buffer carries over between stages.

Park: text vs figure inconsistencies. 4 s vs 5 s per speed (Fig 4); '3 min 30 s' vs 5 x 30 s (p6); 'hip-knee' vs hip-knee-ankle power (p7 vs Fig 9); bilateral vs unilateral student input (p3 vs p4-5); 4.3 kg simulated vs 4.5 kg hardware mass.

Choi: the no-exo baseline's training (base policy or matched fine-tune) and its device mass are unspecified (a shared bar in Fig 4b suggests no device mass). The reward change (10x effort, 5x looser tracking) and 150M extra steps are therefore confounded with assistance.

Choi: tau_max is never reported. Fig 3 hip torques reach about 0.2 Nm/kg in running (about 15 Nm at 74.5 kg; derived by eye), above Park's 12 Nm simulation cap. The 1 Hz hip LPF sits below the running stride frequency.

Choi: 'align with state-of-the-art profiles' (abstract) is only partly true. Running hip profiles carry about +0.2 Nm/kg of flexion torque where the extension-only reference is zero. Ankle running profiles carry dorsiflexion-direction torque absent from the plantarflexion-only reference (Fig 3 p6, visual reading).
Choi: tracking and GRF accuracy are in-sample on the single training clip. GRF agreement is largely implied by tracking ID moments and kinematics, though it is presented as emergent.

Choi: 'personalised' rests on one reference subject. Improved symmetry and affected-side-biased assistance follow from tracking a mirrored healthy reference, so they are expected rather than emergent.

Choi: the metabolic probe is both the reward term and the evaluation metric. No seeds or variance are reported. Ref [40] (Kim et al. 2019, an experimental exosuit study) is cited as 'musculoskeletal simulation' (p6). 'Next four reference frames' conflicts with k = 1..5 (p3). Table II weight signs conflict with the minus signs in Eq 1.
Both: 'running' reaches only 2.2 m/s (Choi) and walking only 1.5 m/s (Park). The synergy prior (Park) comes from walking data. Neither paper supports sprint-speed claims.
unspecified_details: Park reward: every weight w_(.), the Gaussian widths and flat-band width, the fall threshold, and the scaling of the knee-load and frontal terms. (Walk-RL gives precursor values for vel/effort/rom/fall only.)
Park curriculum: the difficulty-score increments, floor and sampling temperature; the speed-list granularity; episode length and termination; the initial state.

Park SAC: learning_starts, train_freq/gradient_steps, gSDE (used in Walk-RL), activation function, seeds, training hardware and wall-clock, and whether the replay buffer is reused at the stage switch.
Park filter: whether dt in alpha = dt/tau is 5 ms (dynamics) or 25 ms (control); the order of clip and filter; whether the observed 'current exo torque' is raw or filtered.
Park synergies: source subjects, number of strides, normalisation, the NMF rank-selection criterion, and whether the published W equals Walk-RL's 1.5x10x40 matrix.

Park distillation: how a 40 Hz teacher was run or resampled at 100 Hz; dataset size; the split unit (trial vs window); input normalisation; TCN channels, kernel, dilations and receptive field; optimiser, LR and batch; the left-side policy (mirroring, sign conventions).

Park deployment: units of c; order of mass scaling, rate limit, LPF and clip; the low-level motor torque control (current loop, torque constant); IMU sampling and filtering; end-to-end latency; start-up behaviour during the 0.95 s window.

Park evaluation: the % basis (relative to no-exo?); the joint-power definition (biological vs total); episodes per condition; whether Fig 10's simulated curves are teacher or student-in-sim; what the +/- in r and RMSE is taken across; per-participant results.

Choi: tau_max per joint; the breakdown of the 839-dim observation; reference frame rate and interpolation; which of the 12 subjects; the muscles in each weakened group; SAC buffer size and learning_starts; the no-exo baseline definition and its device mass; evaluation cycles, episodes and seeds; gross vs net metabolic (basal term); wall-clock for fine-tunes; whether knee motors were ever enabled.

a_matched_simple_controllers_and_actuato: Copy Park's control design exactly: fork the exo arm and a zero-torque arm from the same stage-1 checkpoint, with identical reward, curriculum, LR reset, step budget and device mass (Table I; p3). Unlike Park, run at least 3 paired seeds per arm. Every simple controller (spline, delayed biological moment, delayed output feedback) should be its own arm under the same rules, with the human policy co-adapting for the same steps.

Park compared the spline and delayed bio-torque references on timing only (Fig 7). Comparing them on the simulated objective through the same actuator model is the missing experiment, and exactly what 'matched simple controllers' should deliver. Their timing anchors: extension peak 9-17% GC, flexion peak 61-71% GC, bio-torque delay 125 ms (p7).

Actuator realism in these papers is minimal. Park: an ideal torque source, 12 Nm clip, first-order LPF tau = 0.1 s and a smoothness penalty; hardware uses tau = 0.15 s and a rate limiter with c = 0.5. Choi: ideal motors, rate clip tau_max per step, and LPF cutoffs of 1 Hz (hip) and 2 Hz (ankle). For a cable-driven hip exosuit, add tension-only channels, pretension or slack, series (textile) compliance, the motor torque-speed and power envelope through the pulley, and a pure transport delay, all calibrated on the lab bench. Neither paper supplies these.

[derived-ours] Filters copied from walking cripple sprint assistance. For a first-order LPF at an assumed ~2.2 Hz sprint stride frequency: tau = 0.1 s gives gain 0.59 and 68 ms lag (15% of the stride); tau = 0.15 s gives gain 0.43 and 81 ms (18%); Choi's 1 Hz hip cutoff gives gain 0.41 and 83 ms (18%). At a ~0.9 Hz walking stride, tau = 0.1 s gives gain 0.87 and 91 ms lag. Model the delay and bandwidth explicitly and sweep them. Do not inherit these constants.

Torque scale: Park's 12 Nm cap is 0.161 Nm/kg at 74.5 kg. Scale by model mass (MyoAssist human about 78.09 kg per the myoassist digest), or set it from the exosuit motor spec. Choi's running hip torques of about 0.2 Nm/kg (derived by eye) exceed that cap.
b_teacher_student_sprint_transfer: Park's template is: privileged SAC teacher -> teacher rollouts at the deploy rate (100 Hz) -> 95-sample history of one thigh mediolateral gyro -> TCN -> unilateral torque -> mass scale -> rate limit -> LPF -> motor. This is the only published end-to-end pipeline in these papers, and it validates waveform shape only.

Sprint-specific problems. (1) The 0.95 s history yields no output for the first 0.95 s (Fig 4 caption). That is fatal for block starts, where the largest measured sprint-exosuit benefit sits (0-100 m; see sprint_evidence_and_baselines digest). Use a shorter window, a start-phase prior or a padded history. (2) The student has no speed or phase input, so it must infer acceleration vs max-velocity phase from gyro history alone. Test this closed-loop in simulation. (3) The gyro agreement (r 0.55 at 1.2 m/s walking) must be re-measured at sprint speeds, where thigh angular velocities and soft-tissue artefacts are far larger. (4) Evaluate the student closed-loop in simulation against the teacher on the actual objective (200 m time), not just R^2. Use DAgger if covariate shift appears. (5) Split by whole trials, phases and seeds to prevent window leakage.

SMAT's exo actor already observes only hip angles and velocities plus past commands (smat_original_and_extended digest, recipe step 5), so a SMAT-style exo policy may deploy without distillation where hip encoders exist. A cable exosuit with thigh IMUs measures thigh, not hip, angle unless a pelvis IMU is added. Decide the sensor set before training the sprint teacher, and log simulated sensor signals at the IMU site in every rollout.
Do not carry Park's walking synergies (NMF of walking MocoInverse activations, scaled 1.5x in Walk-RL) into a sprint human. They constrain the action space to walking coordination.

Choi's route to a running human is imitation: a DeepMimic reward, then a fine-tune with loosened tracking and a stronger effort term. It reaches only 2.2 m/s. If used for a sprinter, give the matched no-exo fine-tune the identical reward change.
c_throughput_planning: Choi's 600M steps in about 48 h used 96 Hyfydy CPU envs on a 24-core desktop CPU, so it anchors a CPU physics stack, not our GPU. It does not transfer to MuJoCo MyoAssist on a 64-core EPYC. See throughput_notes for the arithmetic.

Park's budget is 1.5e8 env steps per full two-branch pipeline (derived), with no wall-clock reported. It is small next to SMAT's 547M, so Park-style matched-arm experiments are the cheap ones to multiply over seeds.

Hyfydy reference runs (Walk-RL, Choi-style) need a licence, and the EUR 995/yr personal non-commercial tier is capped at 24 CPU cores (hyfydy.com/purchase, fetched 2026-09-23). Using the full server costs EUR 2,000/yr (personal HPC) or EUR 4,000/yr (academic lab).
code_and_assets: Walk-RL (main e5c55db, 2025-12-19): SCONE/Hyfydy gym wrappers (H2190UnevenVelocityWrapper for training on random terrain, H2190RampVelocityWrapper for fixed-slope evaluation), SB3 SAC train.py, rollout.py, TensorBoard analysis scripts, and a 10x40 synergy matrix (synergy/synergy.py, x1.5). Also H2190v2k .hfd variants (plain/S2/uphill/downhill), .scone scenarios, a terrain generator (terrains themselves absent), and vendored sconegym 0.2.0 (pyproject says MIT, LICENSE file is Apache-2.0). No exo actuator, TCN, datasets, checkpoints or README.

Walk-RL NMSM branch (a092f8d, 2025-12-18): synergy/synergy_results_arr.py with the 10x40 matrix and a '251204_NMSM_Inv_6' 6-synergy matrix, described as NMF of MocoInverse activations via an unreleased sto2synergy_mat.py. Also a hangman test script and an install-order note: gym 0.13 via sconegym requirements, stable-baselines3[extra]==2.6.0, torch 2.7.0 cu128, numpy 1.26.*, scikit-learn 1.6.1, shimmy 2.0.0, pyyaml.

The model/H2190_S2.scone and H2190v2k_S2.hfd files are upstream sconegym variants (identical copies ship in sconegym-main/sconegym/data-v1). They set enable_dof_actuators = 0, add a lumbar joint motor (stiffness 10, damping 10) and muscle_force_multiplier = 2. 'S2' is not Park's curriculum stage 2.

[argued-ours] Walk-RL matches the companion paper arXiv 2603.10474 (Park, E. Choi, J. Ahn, J. Ahn; v2 2026-05-28): synergy vs unconstrained control, 0.7-1.8 m/s, +/-6 deg grades, uneven terrain. That paper's project page is named 'WebHomepage__Walk-RL' and says 'Code (Coming Soon)', 'Dataset (Coming Soon)'. So Walk-RL is the precursor human controller, not a partial exo release.

Related lab repos (MetaMobilityLabCMU): speed-adaptive-agent (MIT; Park ref [35], cyclic speed curriculum source) and MeMo-Hyfydy-Workshop (2026-03, H0918 sconegym workshop). Neither contains exo or TCN code.
Choi: nothing public beyond the project page.

reimplementation_recipe: 0. Scope: this is an independent reconstruction in MuJoCo/MyoAssist. H2190/Hyfydy numbers (90 muscles, compliant tendons, 200 Hz) are not numeric targets; the targets are directions, relative effects and the transfer procedure. Label every inferred choice.

1. Environment: MyoAssist myolegs26 + Hippo_L1 composed per the myoassist_framework digest (planar root; actuators: 26 muscles, then Exo_R, Exo_L). Control at 40 Hz as the Park variant, next to SMAT's 50 Hz. Physics at 1000 or 1200 Hz; record frame_skip.

2. Device mass: add the measured exosuit mass split (Park's hip-exo split was thigh 0.5/0.5, pelvis 2.0, torso 1.3 kg; Choi's was pelvis 1.5, thigh 0.7/0.7 kg) with inertia scaled proportionally. Add it to every arm, including the zero-torque arm.

3. One actuator module shared by every controller. Commanded torque at control rate -> optional pure delay d -> clip to +/-T_max (Park: 12 Nm * m_model/74.5) -> slew limit c per 10 ms (Park hardware c = 0.5, read literally as Nm per step, i.e. 50 Nm/s; log the choice) -> first-order LPF with alpha = dt/tau, or exact 1 - exp(-dt/tau), at physics dt (tau 0.1 s sim-faithful, 0.15 s hardware-faithful; sweep 0-0.15 s) -> hip joint torque. Exosuit variant: split into unidirectional flexion and extension channels (tension >= 0), add pretension/slack, series stiffness and a motor torque-speed envelope from the lab bench. Choi variant: clip [-1,1] -> +/-tau_max, rate clip tau_max per step, 1 Hz hip LPF.

4. Park teacher (single joint policy, one variant beside SMAT's two agents): SB3 SAC MlpPolicy [512,512,256] for actor and critic. gamma 0.99, buffer 3e6 (see RAM note), batch 512, tau 0.005, ent_coef 'auto_0.1', LR linear 1e-3->0 in stage 1, reset to 5e-4->0 in stage 2. Park used 30 envs; optional gSDE as in Walk-RL. Actions: 26 excitations ([-1,1] -> 0.5*(a+1)) plus 2 normalised hip torques. Synergies are optional at 13 muscles per leg; treat NMF synergies as a variant. Observation: the Walk-RL layout adapted to MyoAssist (fibre length, velocity, force, excitation and activation; head orientation and angular velocity; feet relative to pelvis; joint positions with pelvis translation zeroed; joint velocities; GRF/BW; COM velocity; target speed) plus normalised current exo torques. VecNormalize on observations only.

5. Park reward: start from the Walk-RL weights: 10*r_vel - 0.1*sum(a^2) - 25*rom - 250*fall. r_vel = exp(-0.06*(v_x - band edge)^2/0.07^2) with a +/-0.05 m/s flat band, times exp(-0.06*v_z^2/0.1^2), times head-angular-velocity Gaussians with sigma (0.6, 0.65, 1.4) rad/s. Add w_sm*sum((u_t - u_{t-1})^2) and w_knee*max(0, F_knee - 3 BW). Both weights are unknown, so sweep them over at least 3 log-spaced values chosen before the sweep. The frontal term does not apply in a planar model. rom: knee > 0 plus lumbar outside [-30, 2.5] deg (paper) or [-20, 10] deg (code); record which.

6. Park curriculum: stage 1 with the exo clamped (50M steps in Park). Stage 2 forks two runs from the same checkpoint (exo vs zero-torque; 50M each in Park) with the same seeds and the same LR reset. Slopes -5..+5 deg (11 values) via difficulty scores: +delta on fall, -delta on success, floor s_min, p proportional to score; delta and s_min are unspecified, so choose and record them. Speeds follow the cyclic list 0.7->1.5->0.7 in 0.1 steps, advanced per episode. Implement slope by tilting the floor or rotating gravity in the planar model. Run at least 3 paired seeds per arm; report paired differences with CIs.

7. Park metrics, defined before running: mean activation over all muscles in a 15 s steady segment, at 9 speeds x 3 slopes. Mean positive biological joint power = positive part of (net moment - exo torque) x joint velocity, averaged over bilateral hip, knee and ankle. % change = 100*(noexo - exo)/noexo, with sign stated. Also sagittal angle and moment RMSE and r against Reznick et al. 2021 at 0.8/1.0/1.2 m/s.

8. Matched simple controllers, each through the step-3 module with the human co-adapted for equal steps and equal seeds: (i) zero-torque plus mass; (ii) gait-phase spline with extension peak at 9-17% GC and flexion peak at 61-71% GC, amplitude matched to the RL controller's RMS torque; (iii) delayed biological hip moment, k*M_hip(t - 125 ms), clipped to T_max; (iv) delayed output feedback on thigh angles as a sensor-realistic baseline. Tune (ii)-(iv) with a fixed, pre-declared budget (e.g. CMA-ES) on tuning seeds, then evaluate on fresh seeds.

9. Student (Park): roll out the teacher at 100 Hz (zero-order-hold the 40/50 Hz command; log raw and filtered torque). Log femur mediolateral angular velocity in the femur frame at the IMU site, plus a noise, bias and misalignment model. Use 95-sample windows with target = raw right-hip command / T_max. Split by whole trials (speed x slope x seed blocks). TCN, our default (not Park's): causal dilated Conv1d, kernel 3, dilations 1-32, 32-64 channels, Adam 1e-3, batch 512, 5-20 epochs with early stopping. Mirror for the left side after checking signs. Report open-loop R^2 and RMSE per condition and closed-loop retention of the teacher's effect with the student driving the device. Include the 0.95 s start-up gap.

10. Choi-style imitation (optional route to running or sprinting humans): MyoAssist imitation env with the DeepMimic terms and Choi Table II gains (base k: pos -2.0, vel -0.05, root -500, ee -80, torq -2.0; w: 0.25/0.1/0.15/0.25/0.25). Effort: Umberger/Uchida-type probe with w 3e-5 (base) and 3e-4 (fine-tune). Excitation smoothness weight 1.0. Reference-state init; 10 s (250-step) episodes at 25 Hz; terminate at 0.4 m root error. SAC per Table III (gamma 0.95, batch 256, LR 3e-4 linear, tau 0.02, train_freq 4, gradient_steps 4). Exo fine-tune: 150M steps with tracking k/5, w_eff x10 and w_exo 0.2*0.5*sum|tau|/tau_max. Always run the matched no-exo fine-tune with the identical reward change, steps and mass.

11. RAM guard: an SB3 replay buffer stores obs and next_obs as float32. At 3e6 transitions, 515-dim observations need about 12.4 GB, over the 12 GB experiment lane. Use optimize_memory_usage=True, a 1e6 buffer, or a smaller observation, and measure per-env memory before choosing the env count.
12. Provenance: log seeds, repo commits, MJCF/XML sha256, the actuator-module parameters, filter discretisation, metric definitions and the Walk-RL/paper choice made for every unspecified item above.
throughput_notes: [reported] Choi: 96 parallel envs, 600M steps, about 48 h on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 + Intel Ultra 9 285K (p4 Sec II-D-1). [derived-ours] That is about 3,470 env-steps/s aggregate, about 36 steps/s per env, or about 1.45x real time per env at 25 Hz. With 200 Hz physics that is about 28k physics steps/s across the machine. Hyfydy physics runs on the CPU; the 285K has 24 cores (8P+16E per Intel's spec, not stated in the paper), and the GPU only runs SAC updates.

[derived-ours] SB3 counts train_freq in vectorised-env steps. With 96 envs, train_freq 4 and gradient_steps 4 give one gradient update per 96 transitions (UTD about 0.0104), about 6.25M updates over 600M steps at batch 256. This low UTD explains how 600M steps fit in 48 h. A higher UTD would cut env throughput.

[reported] Choi fine-tunes: 150M steps per device condition (Table III), wall-clock not reported. [derived-ours] At the same rate each takes about 12 h, and the hip, ankle and impaired variants add 25% or more per model.

[reported] Park: 30 envs, 1e8 steps per branch, 40 Hz control, 200 Hz dynamics; no hardware or wall-clock reported. [derived-ours] 1.5e8 env steps per full pipeline is about 1,042 h of simulated walking.

[from sibling digests, not re-measured here] Server sail-gpu: EPYC 9535 (64C/128T), 30 GB RAM, one RTX 5090; the experiment lane defaults to at most 48 threads and 12 GB. MyoAssist myolegs26+Hippo env.step measured at 2.36 ms (50 Hz control / 1000 Hz physics), about 420 steps/s per core env-only (myoassist_framework.json). [derived-ours] 40 CPU envs could therefore supply about 10-17k steps/s before learner and IPC overhead. A Park-style 1.5e8-step two-arm pipeline would take about 3-8 h, and hundreds of seeds or arms become feasible only as stage-2 forks off shared stage-1 checkpoints. All of this must be measured.

[derived-ours] Replay memory: 3e6 transitions x obs_dim x 4 B x 2 is 12.4 GB for 515 dims (Walk-RL layout) and 20.1 GB for 839 dims (Choi). SAC at Park or Choi buffer sizes collides with the 30 GB RAM cap once 40-60 env processes are running.

[vendor page, fetched 2026-09-23] Hyfydy licences: personal non-commercial EUR 995/yr (max 24 CPU cores); personal non-commercial HPC EUR 2,000/yr (no core limit); academic lab EUR 4,000/yr; academic department EUR 8,000/yr. Running Walk-RL or Choi-style Hyfydy baselines on all 64 cores needs the HPC or lab tier.
rival_explanations: Park timing: the 103/166 ms lags may be mostly the tau = 0.1 s filter (about 91 ms phase delay at a 0.9 Hz stride; derived) rather than a learned phase-dependent strategy. Test: retrain the teacher at tau in {0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15} s and see whether the lag tracks tau.
Park effort effects (1.1-3.4% activation): these may lie within the seed-to-seed variance of two separately trained SAC policies. Test: at least 3 paired seeds per arm.

Park speed trend (r 0.98): it holds on 9 slope-averaged points (derived). It may partly reflect larger absolute effort, and larger torque use, at higher speed rather than better-matched assistance. The effect is not robust once slopes are pooled (r about 0.69 over 27 points, derived).

Park sim-to-real agreement: both signals are smooth, filtered, phase-locked functions of thigh motion. Similar walking kinematics plus low-pass filtering can give high r whatever the assistance quality. r ignores amplitude, and the signals are commands, not delivered torque. Uphill r 0.98 vs downhill 0.66 may reflect signal size (large, simple ascent profiles vs small descent profiles) rather than 'training-distribution representation', for which no evidence is shown.
Park 'without hardware tuning': the hardware filter (0.15 s) and rate limiter change the waveform, and could have been chosen after pilot testing (not stated).

Choi metabolic reductions: if the no-exo baseline is the base policy, the fine-tuned exo policies differ in reward (10x effort weight, looser tracking), in training (+150M steps) and in mass, not only in assistance. The reward change alone could lower probe cost by freeing the gait from the reference. Test: a matched no-exo fine-tune.

Choi larger savings at higher speeds: consistent with larger absolute torques (tau_max unknown; hip up to about 0.2 Nm/kg in running) and a 1 Hz filter that interacts differently with stride frequency. Not necessarily better timing.

Choi impaired results: asymmetric assistance and improved symmetry are expected from tracking a symmetric healthy reference with a weakened side, so they are not independent evidence of clinical validity.
Choi GRF fidelity: largely implied by tracking kinematics plus inverse-dynamics joint moments, so it is not an independent emergent validation.
ideas_sparked: Make the Park-style matched zero-torque fork the default control for every stage transition in our SMAT reconstruction, with paired seeds. Use the same fork rule for each simple controller, so co-adaptation is matched.

Run a 'filter-attribution' mini-study: sweep the actuator time constant and delay, and measure whether the learned timing and benefit move. This is cheap, directly tests a published interpretation, and sets the realistic-actuator requirements for the exosuit.

Add a distillability gate for any sprint teacher: after training, fit a single-thigh-gyro student and require closed-loop retention of at least X% of the teacher's 200 m time gain in simulation before calling the controller deployable (X declared in advance).

Report both effort proxies on identical rollouts: Park-style mean activation and positive power, and a Choi-style Umberger/Uchida probe (as 01_PAPERS.md line 310 already proposes). Exo benefit can depend on the proxy.

Adopt Park's gyro-axis agreement check as an acceptance test for the simulated sensor model: per-axis r and RMSE of simulated vs real thigh gyro. Extend it to sprint phases (start, acceleration, max velocity) once the lab records IMU data.

kb_digest_reused.accurate: Largely accurate against the PDF and the current GitHub state. Confirmed: all Park numbers quoted (4.3 vs 4.5 kg, 12/18 Nm, 0.1/0.15 s, c = 0.5, 95 samples, r 0.55 / RMSE 96, r 0.82/0.98/0.83/0.66, the 74.5 kg scaling); Walk-RL main e5c55db (2025-12-19) with pushed_at 2026-06-26; Learning-Hip-Exo b8ec147 as website-only; the project page's ramp-descent failure sentence; the listed text inconsistencies.
corrections: 'Inspected H2190 stage-2 scenario disables DOF actuators' misreads upstream sconegym naming. H2190_S2.scone is byte-identical to sconegym-main/sconegym/data-v1/H2190_S2.scone, and 'S2' is not Park's curriculum stage 2. The training env loads random-terrain scenarios built on H2190v2k.hfd. The underlying point (no exo actuator anywhere; only muscle excitations emitted) stands.

The audit missed branch NMSM (a092f8d, 2025-12-18): a 6-synergy '251204_NMSM_Inv_6' matrix, symmetry off, batch 512, tau 0.01, LR 5e-4, plus an install-order note (SB3[extra] 2.6.0, torch 2.7.0 cu128, numpy 1.26.*, scikit-learn 1.6.1, shimmy 2.0.0). The audit's 'no dependency lock' is still true for main.

Walk-RL most likely belongs to the companion synergy paper arXiv 2603.10474 (project page 'WebHomepage__Walk-RL', code 'Coming Soon'). That explains the ind/syn configs, the 0.7-1.6 m/s schedule, the +/-6 deg uneven terrain and the 10-seed scripts. So it is a precursor human controller, not a partial exo release.

The public reward differs from the paper, not only in hyperparameters. It has 4 terms (velocity x head-angvel x vertical-velocity Gaussians, effort, ROM, fall) with weights 10/-0.1/-25/-250. Head orientation is not in the product, lumbar bounds are [-20, 10] deg vs [-30, 2.5], and there are no knee-load, frontal or smoothness terms. The code also enables gSDE, ReLU, learning_starts 1e4, train_freq 4 and gradient_steps 4, none of which the paper states.

On the gyro axis: the audit correctly notes the negative correlations of the other axes but omits that x and y had lower RMSE (41.2, 60.9 deg/s) than the chosen z (96.0). Selection was on correlation only.
It omits the distillation losses (validation MSE 6.54e-2 normalised). These imply aggregate fit far below the showcased R^2 0.93.
It omits two further inconsistencies: 'hip-knee' power (text) vs hip-knee-ankle (Fig 9 caption), and ramp-descent activation '-2.2%', which under Fig 9's sign convention is an increase.
Stage 2 means two 50M-step branches, so a full pipeline is 1.5e8 env steps, not 1e8.

kb_digest_reused.accurate: The numbers are accurate: 600M steps in about 48 h with an RTX 5090 (p4, Table III), and 6.95% hip saving in running (p6, Fig 4b). The framing is partly misleading.
corrections: The 48 h covers only the 600M-step base imitation policy. Each 150M-step fine-tune (hip, ankle, impaired) is extra and untimed.

It is not a 'compute anchor on our exact GPU'. Hyfydy physics runs on a 24-core Intel Core Ultra 9 285K CPU with 96 envs; the RTX 5090 only runs SB3 SAC updates at a low update-to-data ratio (about 0.01, derived).

6.95% is a metabolic-probe (Umberger/Uchida) reduction averaged over 2.0 and 2.2 m/s jogging, not sprinting. It is measured against a no-exo baseline whose training and mass are unspecified. Ankle assistance reached 13.81% in the same runs, so 'only' is framing.
The knee motors exist in the action space, but only hip and ankle policies were trained and reported.
